findings.title: Desktop command producer hides both shell acquisition and background child failures
findings.reproduction: Run actual Gestures.execute_action(mic_mute_toggle,tap_3) with recording os.execute returning nil/exit126 or throwing: no warning/error. Then run its exact command through a real POSIX shell with only a scratch fake pactl that writes a reached marker and exits37: the child failure is discarded, and there is no error diagnostic. Healthy exit control also executes once. No actual audio device or user session is used.
findings.root_cause: linux/modules/gestures/manager.lua run_background wraps os.execute(cmd .. " 2>/dev/null &") in an ignored pcall, so acquisition failure is lost and successful shell background dispatch has no retained child status/error channel. SystemActions fixed commands and multiple direct/handler actions share this producer.
findings.silent_failure: stderr is redirected to /dev/null and no completion owner exists. execute_action=true only acknowledges a nonempty action name by its documented contract; it is not reinterpreted as a terminal success receipt.
findings.regression_test: Exercise the actual public dispatcher and native owned child boundary with construction/launch refusal, nonzero exit, stderr, healthy exit, cancellation and late callbacks. Require observable refusal without blocking the grabbed-keyboard daemon; do not replace asynchronous dispatch with synchronous waits.
findings.basis: real module+recording acquisition boundary, plus real POSIX shell and scratch fake native tool

findings.title: Overlapping accepted theme toggles lose one read-modify-write update
findings.reproduction: Dispatch toggle_dark_mode twice through the real public manager with independently named bindings. Real POSIX background shells use a private fake gsettings with quoted GVariant output and a read barrier: both read default and write prefer-dark. Sequential control returns default after two toggles. No actual desktop preference is touched.
findings.root_cause: The fixed COMMANDS.toggle_dark_mode shell reads GNOME color-scheme then derives and writes its opposite. The manager admits separate gestures/keyboard actions and launches independent background shells without an operation owner or serialization across this read-modify-write interval.
findings.silent_failure: Both dispatches are accepted and both child commands complete, but one requested state transition is lost. The public true acknowledgment is not interpreted as completed native success.
findings.regression_test: Exercise two independent public bindings with a controlled native read barrier, assert two accepted toggles compose to the initial state, and retain sequential, read-refusal, write-refusal and cancellation controls without blocking the input daemon.
findings.basis: Real public manager, real POSIX shells and private native-tool fixture; actual GNOME and other OS atomicity remain unqualified.
